 --> GIFT Nifty falls 100 pts, signals weak start for Sensex, Nifty despite Asian, Wall Street rallies; Fed in focus
 GIFT Nifty was trading down more than 100 points on Tuesday morning, amid contrasting signals from a global technology-led rebound, suggesting a cautious opening for Sensex and Nifty. Crude oil prices and geopolitical headlines are likely to remain important drivers of sentiment. 
 Shaleen Agrawal 
 October 27, 2026 / 08:06 IST Share --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 Share Markets Updates | Sensex, Nifty, GIFT Nifty Today Sensex and Nifty are likely to open lower on Tuesday.
 GIFT Nifty fell over 100 points, signaling a weak start.
 Asian markets surge as AI optimism lifts tech stocks.

 Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty are likely to open lower on Tuesday, with GIFT Nifty falling over 100 points, signalling a weak start despite a sharp rally across Asian markets and overnight gains on Wall Street. A rebound in global technology stocks, driven by renewed optimism around artificial intelligence following Anthropic's IPO filing, has lifted global sentiment. However, elevated crude oil prices, geopolitical uncertainty and caution ahead of the US Federal Reserve's policy decision could weigh on Indian equities.
 GIFT Nifty was trading at 22,669 around 7:45 am, down 104.5 points, or 0.46 percent. Indian equities snapped a four-session losing streak on Monday, with the Sensex gaining 482.92 points, or 0.66 percent, to 73,606.75 and the Nifty advancing 153.20 points, or 0.68 percent, to 22,753.20. Foreign institutional investors sold equities worth Rs 1,462 crore, while domestic institutions bought shares worth Rs 2,609 crore, extending their buying streak to ten consecutive sessions.
 Asian markets surge as AI optimism lifts technology stocks
 Asian equities rallied on Tuesday as Anthropic's much-anticipated IPO filing revived investor appetite for artificial intelligence-related stocks ahead of major technology earnings and central bank policy decisions.
 Share Markets Live Updates | Sensex, Nifty, GIFT Nifty Today 
 South Korea's Kospi jumped more than 4 percent in early trading, while Japan's Nikkei gained 1.9 percent. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan rose 1.2 percent. US equity futures also traded higher, with Nasdaq futures gaining 0.4 percent after US semiconductor stocks rallied 2.8 percent overnight, recording their biggest one-day advance in a month.

 Wall Street rebounds as Anthropic IPO filing boosts sentiment
 US equities closed higher on Monday, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq recovering after consecutive weekly declines as Anthropic's IPO filing supported renewed buying in AI-related stocks.
 The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 146.42 points, or 0.28 percent, to 52,361.58, while the S&P 500 gained 53.09 points, or 0.70 percent, to 7,676.77. The Nasdaq Composite advanced 214.04 points, or 0.83 percent, to 26,169.38.
 Investors are now looking ahead to a busy week of market-moving events, including the Federal Reserve's policy statement on Wednesday, US economic growth and inflation data on Thursday, and a series of major corporate earnings announcements.
 Brent slips but remains near six-month highs
 Crude oil prices edged lower on Tuesday as hopes of a possible resolution to the US-Israeli war on Iran eased immediate supply concerns, although continued attacks on Saudi Arabia kept geopolitical risks elevated.
 Brent crude futures fell 66 cents, or 0.57 percent, to $115.15 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate declined 44 cents, or 0.43 percent, to $101.32 a barrel. Yet, Brent remained close to six-month highs, reflecting continued concerns.
 Fed policy, geopolitical developments to guide Indian markets
 Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, said the near-term direction of domestic equities is likely to remain sensitive to geopolitical developments, crude oil price movements and signals from the US Federal Reserve. He expects volatility to persist as investors balance external risks against the possibility of a sustained recovery in market sentiment.
 The Federal Reserve's policy announcement on Wednesday will be a major event for global markets, with investors looking for indications of the future interest-rate trajectory.
